questions.question: Distinguish between economic carrying capacity and physical carrying capacity .
questions.solution_html:

  • or inflation of local goods and services is called economic carrying capacity.

  • accommodate at a time in a destination.

questions.question: Compare the ecological importance of rivers, seas, and lakes. Discuss how / eco-tourists can engage in sustainable activities in these environments while conserving the flora and fauna.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the ecological importance of rivers, seas, and lakes. Discuss how eco-tourists can
  • engage in sustainable activities in these environments while conserving the flora and fauna.
  • Rivers support freshwater biodiversity, transport nutrients, recharge groundwater, and sustain forests
  • wetlands, and agriculture.
  • Seas regulate global climate, store carbon, support marine life, and maintain the world’s largest
  • ecosystems such as coral reefs.
  • Lakes act as freshwater reservoirs, support aquatic species, balance local climates, and provide habitats
  • for birds and fish.
  • Eco-tourists can engage sustainably by avoiding pollution, minimizing waste, and using non-motorised
  • activities,follow marked trails, respect wildlife distances, avoid disturbing habitats,supporting local
  • conservation programs, choosing eco-friendly accommodations, learning about local ecosystems
questions.final_answer: conservation programs, choosing eco-friendly accommodations, learning about local ecosystems
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Examine the various alternative tourism with appropriate examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the various alternative tourism with appropriate examples.
  • Alternative tourism refers to forms of travel that differ from conventional mass tourism. It focuses on
  • sustainable, authentic, and environmentally or culturally sensitive experiences, often promoting local
  • development and minimizing negative impacts.
  •  Ecotourism. Eg: Gavi Ecotourism in Kerala, Periyar Tiger Reserve.
  •  Adventure Tourism. Eg: River rafting in Rishikesh, trekking in Himachal Pradesh.
  •  Cultural Tourism. Eg: Visiting forts and palaces in Rajasthan, attending Theyyamperformances
  •  Rural Tourism. Eg: Kumbalangi Model Village in Kerala.
  •  Wildlife Tourism. Eg: Safari tours in Kaziranga National Park or Bandipur Tiger Reserve.
  •  Medical Tourism. Eg: Kerala’s Ayurveda treatments; medical hospitals attracting international
  • patients to Chennai etc...
questions.final_answer: patients to Chennai etc
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Compare the ecological importance of rivers, seas, and lakes. Discuss how / eco-tourists can engage in sustainable activities in these environments while conserving the flora and fauna.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the ecological importance of rivers, seas, and lakes. Discuss how eco-tourists can
  • engage in sustainable activities in these environments while conserving the flora and fauna.
  • Rivers support freshwater biodiversity, transport nutrients, recharge groundwater, and sustain forests
  • wetlands, and agriculture.
  • Seas regulate global climate, store carbon, support marine life, and maintain the world’s largest
  • ecosystems such as coral reefs.
  • Lakes act as freshwater reservoirs, support aquatic species, balance local climates, and provide habitats
  • for birds and fish.
  • Eco-tourists can engage sustainably by avoiding pollution, minimizing waste, and using non-motorised
  • activities,follow marked trails, respect wildlife distances, avoid disturbing habitats,supporting local
  • conservation programs, choosing eco-friendly accommodations, learning about local ecosystems
questions.final_answer: conservation programs, choosing eco-friendly accommodations, learning about local ecosystems

questions.question: Examine the various alternative tourism with appropriate examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the various alternative tourism with appropriate examples.
  • Alternative tourism refers to forms of travel that differ from conventional mass tourism. It focuses on
  • sustainable, authentic, and environmentally or culturally sensitive experiences, often promoting local
  • development and minimizing negative impacts.
  •  Ecotourism. Eg: Gavi Ecotourism in Kerala, Periyar Tiger Reserve.
  •  Adventure Tourism. Eg: River rafting in Rishikesh, trekking in Himachal Pradesh.
  •  Cultural Tourism. Eg: Visiting forts and palaces in Rajasthan, attending Theyyamperformances
  •  Rural Tourism. Eg: Kumbalangi Model Village in Kerala.
  •  Wildlife Tourism. Eg: Safari tours in Kaziranga National Park or Bandipur Tiger Reserve.
  •  Medical Tourism. Eg: Kerala’s Ayurveda treatments; medical hospitals attracting international
  • patients to Chennai etc...
